p: The east side of Leeds is easy to reach by road, which makes Garforth a handy meeting point if you're gathering a group from different parts of Yorkshire. Book the slot first, then send everyone the time with a bit of buffer added, because there's always one who gets lost.

Before you head over, everyone climbing will need a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and it saves time to fill it in online. Check the age guidance when you book, as there's normally a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for younger children. Plan on a couple of hours for the whole visit.

To get the most out of your time on the walls, start with an easy warm-up, then tackle the timed walls, and finish with the big jumps when confidence is high. If anyone's anxious about letting go, try a low climb first. Once they've felt how slowly the auto-belay lowers them, the fear usually melts away.

Fancy more once you're done? Lotherton Hall near Aberford, a few miles north-east of Garforth, has a historic house, a bird garden and big gardens to explore. RSPB St Aidan's, on former opencast mining land near Swillington, is a great spot for a wander and some birdwatching, with wide paths and big skies. Bring trainers you don't mind getting a bit muddy.
